demo_input.text: The secret to a happy life is

expected_output_preview.generated_text: The secret to a happy life is finding balance, surrounding yourself with positive people, and pursuing your passions.

beginner_explanation: GPT is like an auto-complete on steroids. You give it the beginning of a sentence, and it predicts what comes next, one word at a time, writing entire paragraphs that sound human-like.
advanced_explanation: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) uses a Transformer decoder architecture with autoregressive language modeling: predict next token given all previous tokens. It uses masked self-attention (causal attention) where each token can only attend to previous tokens, not future ones. Pre-training maximizes L = Σ log P(t_i | t_{<i}). GPT-2 has 1.5B parameters; GPT-3 has 175B. Temperature controls randomness: P_softmax = softmax(logits / T). Lower T = more deterministic; higher T = more random.

formula_cards.title: Autoregressive Language Modeling
formula_cards.explanation: GPT maximizes the log-likelihood of each token given all previous tokens. This is causal (left-to-right) modeling.
formula_cards.example: For 'happy life is', model computes P('happy'|'The'), P('life'|'The happy'), P('is'|'The happy life')

formula_cards.title: Causal Self-Attention (Masked)
formula_cards.formula: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax((QK^T + M)/√d_k)V, where M_{ij} = -∞ if j > i
formula_cards.explanation: Causal masking M prevents attention to future tokens. Each token only attends to itself and previous tokens.
formula_cards.example: When processing 'life' (position 3), it can attend to 'The', 'happy', 'life' but NOT 'is' (future)

formula_cards.title: Temperature Sampling
formula_cards.explanation: Temperature T controls randomness. T=1 is standard softmax; T<1 is sharper (more confident); T>1 is flatter (more random).

variables.logits_i: raw model output for token i

formula_cards.example: T=0.7: 'happy' with logit 3.0 → P=0.6; T=2.0: same logit → P=0.35 (more random)

step_explanations.title: Validate Prompt
step_explanations.description: Check that the input prompt is non-empty and within model's context window.

input_preview.text: The secret to a happy life is

step_explanations.why_it_matters: GPT needs a valid prompt to start generation. Context window limit is typically 1024-4096 tokens.

step_explanations.title: Tokenize with Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)
step_explanations.description: Split prompt into BPE subword tokens and convert to token IDs for the model.

input_preview.text: The secret to a happy life is

step_explanations.why_it_matters: BPE handles out-of-vocabulary words. Token IDs are the actual input to the model.

step_explanations.title: Autoregressive Generation (Step 1 to T)
step_explanations.description: At each step, run the Transformer decoder on all previous tokens, predict next token distribution, sample using temperature, and append to sequence.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: This is the core generation loop - the model builds the output one token at a time, each prediction conditioned on all previous tokens.

step_explanations.title: Decode Generated Tokens to Text
step_explanations.description: Convert generated token IDs back to text using the BPE decoder.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: This is the final output that users see - the model's generated continuation of the prompt.

hover_annotations.definition: A mask that prevents the model from attending to future tokens, ensuring autoregressive generation.
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: M_{ij} = -∞ if j > i (future positions get -∞ → softmax gives 0 probability)
hover_annotations.example: When generating token 5, positions 6, 7, 8, ... are masked out (attention = 0)
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Thinking GPT can see future tokens (it can't - causal mask prevents this by design)

hover_annotations.definition: Parameter that controls randomness in sampling. Lower = more deterministic; higher = more random/creative.
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: softmax(logits / T): T<1 sharpens distribution; T>1 flattens it
hover_annotations.example: T=0.1: almost greedy (always picks highest logit); T=2.0: very random output
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Setting T=0 (not actually 0, use argmax instead; T→0 in softmax approaches argmax)

references.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
references.relevance: GPT-2 paper showing that large-scale generative pre-training enables zero-shot task performance.

references.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
references.relevance: GPT-3 paper demonstrating in-context learning with 175B parameters.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: GPT writes text one word at a time, always looking at what it already wrote to decide what comes next. Like predictive text on your phone, but much smarter.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Use a simple prompt. Show how changing temperature affects creativity vs. coherence.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: GPT uses a Transformer decoder with causal (masked) self-attention. It predicts next token: P(t_i|t_{<i}). Temperature T controls sampling randomness.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Causal mask ensures token i only attends to positions ≤ i. BPE tokenization handles OOV. Autoregressive: generate one token at a time.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: GPT demonstrated that scaling autoregressive LMs enables few-shot in-context learning (Brown et al., 2020). Limitations: no bidirectional context, expensive inference (autoregressive can't parallelize). Led to GPT-3, GPT-4, and the modern LLM era.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Limitations: quadratic attention, no bidirectional context (worse for understanding tasks), autoregressive bottleneck. Alternatives: encoder-decoder (T5), non-autoregressive generation.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: GPT-2: 1.5B params, O(n²·d) per generation step. Use HuggingFace. For faster inference, use caching (KV cache) to avoid recomputing past keys/values.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Complexity: O(L×n²×d) without cache; O(L×n×d) with KV cache. API: transformers.GPT2LMHeadModel, transformers.pipeline('text-generation').

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: GPT introduced the modern LLM paradigm. Show how autoregressive generation differs from bidirectional encoding (BERT).
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Quiz: Why can't GPT see future tokens? Exercise: Compare greedy (T→0) vs. creative (T=1.0) generation. Discuss: Why is GPT good for generation but not understanding?

research_context: GPT-2 (Radford et al., 2019) showed that large-scale generative pre-training enables zero-shot generalization. GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020) demonstrated few-shot in-context learning with 175B parameters, launching the modern LLM era. These models use purely autoregressive (left-to-right) generation.

teaching_notes.summary: GPT uses a Transformer decoder with causal attention to generate text autoregressively, one token at a time.
quiz_questions: Why does GPT use causal (masked) attention instead of bidirectional?
What does temperature control in sampling, and how do you set it for greedy vs. creative generation?
Why can't GPT do bidirectional understanding like BERT?
classroom_demo_tips: Show generation step-by-step with token predictions at each step
Visualize causal attention mask as a lower-triangular matrix
common_misconceptions: GPT understands what it's writing (false - it models statistical patterns, not meaning)
More parameters always means better generation (false - can lead to repetition or hallucination without proper tuning)
